transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what really scared me enough to make an appointment is... I just keep thinking it would be easier if I didn’t wake up. And lately, um, sometimes when I’m driving home from the clinic, I actually catch myself wondering what would happen if I just didn’t turn the wheel. It frightened me to realize I was thinking that way, so... that's why I'm here today.
How long have you been having these thoughts and feelings of wanting to not wake up?

Well, I'd say it's been going on for about a month now. We recently took in a relative, and... it's just been this intense up-and-down crisis around that whole situation. That's really when these feelings started getting so bad.
Over this past month, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Yes, I have. Um, I haven’t even touched my camera lately. I haven't checked the bird feeders with any real interest, or... or even cared about what’s coming up in the garden. It's actually pretty frightening to me, because doing those things... that used to be how I felt like myself.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than normal, along with racing thoughts or impulsive behavior?

Well, yes, actually. Earlier this month... I had a few days where I felt almost electrically upbeat. But then I would just snap at everyone over really tiny things. Like at work, if a medication cup was misplaced, or if there was a sudden change in the morning schedule, I would get so angry. It really didn't feel like my usual self to react that way.
During that period when you felt unusually energetic and irritable, how many days in a row did that last?

Um, I'm not exactly sure, to be honest. I didn't really keep track of how many days it was in a row. Everything has just been such a blur lately with all the stress at home... so I really couldn't give you an exact number.
During those few days when you felt unusually energetic and irritable, did you notice you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt rested and full of energy?

Yes, definitely. During that high-energy stretch, I was sleeping maybe three hours a night. I'd still get up before sunrise feeling completely sharp and ready to go. I just felt like I didn't really need any more rest than that.
Thinking back, do you remember if that unusually energetic, irritable stretch lasted at least four days in a row, or was it shorter than that?

I... I honestly couldn't tell you for sure. I know you're looking for a specific number, but like I said, it's all just been such a blur. It might have been four days, or maybe it was just three. I really didn't track it closely enough to say definitely one way or the other.
During that energetic, irritable stretch, did anyone else—like coworkers or family—comment that you seemed different or unusually keyed up?

No, not that I can remember. I mean, my husband might have said I was a little snappy, but nobody at the clinic said anything about me acting different or being keyed up. If they noticed, they didn't mention it to me.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks of low mood, low energy, and loss of interest—at any other time in your life prior to this past month?

Yes. Actually, it hasn't just been this past month. The... well, the depression has been hanging over me for about 11 months now. This past month is when it made everything feel completely unbearable, but yes, it started way before that.
Can you recall if that high-energy, irritable stretch spanned parts of a single work week, like from one shift to another, or do you remember it crossing into a new week?

I really don't know. Like I was saying before, I just didn't keep track of the days like that. I can't remember if it was in the middle of a week or if it carried over the weekend into the next one. It's just... it's hard to separate the days out when you're looking back at it.
During that high-energy, irritable stretch, did you do anything unusually impulsive or out of character—like impulsive spending, rash decisions, or taking risks you normally wouldn't take?

Yes, I did. I ended up buying a bunch of stuff for the clinic that we didn't strictly need... well, I thought we did at the time. I bought monitoring equipment, some new ramps, bedding, just a lot of supplies on impulse. It all felt urgently necessary right then, like I had to get it immediately. But afterward, I realized I'd put all these charges on the credit card that we really can't cover. It was definitely out of character for me to spend like that without checking our budget first.
Do you remember if that high-energy, irritable period was still going on the next time you had a day off from work, or had it already ended by then?

I really can't say for sure. Like I mentioned, the days all just kind of blur together when I try to think back on it. I don't remember if it lasted until my next day off or if it had stopped before then. I just wasn't paying attention to the timeline like that.
Can you tell me how many days passed between when you first started feeling that high-energy, irritable way and when you made that big purchase of clinic supplies?

I honestly don't know how many days it was. Like I was saying, the whole period is just a blur to me now. I couldn't tell you if I bought all that stuff on the first day I started feeling like that, or if it was a few days into it. I just remember feeling like I had to do it right then, but the exact timeline... I really don't have one.
During those few days when you felt unusually energetic and irritable, were you still feeling sad or without interest in things, or did that low mood lift completely during that time?

I... I really can't say for sure. I know I was mostly just feeling really wired and on edge, but as for whether the sadness was completely gone... I just don't know. Like I said, it's all such a blur now, so it's hard to untangle exactly what I was feeling underneath all that irritability. I just don't remember if the low mood lifted completely or not.

I'm not sure. I don't really have an answer for that. Like I've been saying, my memory of that whole stretch is just really foggy... I wish I could give you more specifics, but I just don't have them.

I honestly couldn't tell you. I know you're looking for specifics, but... like I was just saying, that whole stretch of time is a complete blur to me. I don't remember noticing anything like that. I wish I had a better answer for you, but I just don't.
Even if you can't pinpoint exact days, would you say that high-energy, irritable stretch felt more like it lasted only two or three days, or did it feel like it stretched on for about a week or more?

I really don't know how long it lasted. I know I keep saying that, but I just don't have a clear sense of time for that period. It might have been a few days, it might have been a week... I just can't say for sure. The whole thing is just a blur.
During that energetic, irritable stretch, did your husband or anyone else specifically say you seemed like a different person than usual, even if they didn't use words like 'keyed up'?

I don't think so. Or at least... if my husband did say something like that, I really don't remember it. I know it's probably frustrating that I keep giving you the same answer, but I just don't recall anyone making comments about me acting like a different person. That whole time is just really hazy for me.
I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch that. Could you repeat what you just asked?
Aside from the credit card purchase, did that high-energy period cause any other problems—like issues at work, with your husband, or anything else that you had to deal with afterward?

Well, yeah, it's definitely caused problems. I mean, I've started making mistakes at the clinic, which is... not like me. And I've been avoiding my friends lately. I'm just afraid I'll either snap at someone or just completely fall apart in front of them. And at home... my husband has basically had to take over everything. He's doing the bills, making the meals, and... just trying to keep me safe when my thoughts get really dark.
